title: Northbeam AgriScout — onprem integration scratchpad
content:
Meeting snapshot (2026-02-19) — initial technical intake with Northbeam Agri (AgriScout product):

Attendees: Northbeam: Claire Durn (CTO), Mateo Rios (Head of ML), Anika Shah (Platform). Redwood: Priya (SE), Ethan (Infra Eng), Jun (SRE advisor).

Topline ask: deploy a private Redwood runtime inside customer VPC (air-gapped-ish region), serve a fine-tuned orchard-inspection model (2B-ish) plus a smaller fallback 300M reranker. Key constraints: no raw imagery leaving VPC, KMS-managed keys, audit logs for model calls, <120ms token latency for short prompts (camera -> caption -> label). Throughput: bursts to 120 req/min during harvest windows; steady baseline 10–20/min.

Notes / architecture ideas:
- Two-cluster pattern: primary private cluster (dedicated GPU nodes) for the tuned 2B model; fallback cluster with low-cost quantized 300M in same VPC. Router policy in control plane to prefer local primary, fall back to quantized if queue depth > X or token lat > SLO.
- Network: customer wants private egress disabled. Plan: deploy Redwood Private control-plane agent in a small management subnet that talks to Redwood control-plane only over an allowed management bastion (customer to approve). However, they leaned towards a fully offline bundle for compliance — need to confirm whether we can support an on-prem package without control-plane callbacks for telemetry.
- Storage: telemetry + audit logs should land in S3-compatible object store inside VPC (MinIO or S3 in same cloud account). We will ship log forwarder sidecar. Must support SSE-KMS with customer KMS key.
- Secrets/KMS: must integrate with customer KMS/HSM (they use AWS KMS with external key). Confirm our support for CMKs with external key material.
- Data residency: any embeddings or cached prefixes considered customer data — default should be set to TTL 0 unless they opt-in to prefix caching. If they want caching for latency, document tradeoffs for PII leakage.

Performance considerations & gotchas observed in similar pilots:
- Quantized 2B on A10/A100 across long sequences had higher-than-expected mem fragmentation; suggest early smoke test with produced model artifacts (pt/ggml) to measure memory footprint.
- KV cache benefits only if requests share prefixes (camera -> same device id). Their traffic is per-device, lots of repeated schema, so likely good wins — but need to size object cache and cache invalidation strategy for firmware updates.
- Edge cameras send short 30–80 token prompts after on-device preprocessing. Batching at collector (gateway) yields big CPU savings but increases tail latency. Recommend small adaptive batching (3–5 reqs, 30–50ms hold) as default for harvest windows.
- Model fallback semantics: important to maintain consistent labels across model variants. Need a mapping layer or calibration to normalize outputs from 2B and 300M so product UX doesn't flip.

Security and compliance flags:
- Air-gapped / no internet requirement — ask: is periodic binary sync acceptable? (They asked for weekly approved binary updates via signed bundle.)
- Audit granularity: they asked for per-request token counts, prompt hash, model-id, and user/service principal. Confirm support for prompt hashing (salted) rather than storing raw prompts by default.
- SOC-like requirements: retention window 7 years? (they said audit logs need long retention). We'll propose configurable retention + archival to cold storage — costs to be estimated.

Operational playbook (initial thoughts):
- Deployment phases: 1) PoC quickstart in customer dev VPC with small model serving test data (2–4 nodes, non-prod), 2) Performance baseline run (simulate harvest traffic), 3) Hardened staging with signed bundles + backup/restore test, 4) Production go-live + canary traffic ramp.
- Monitoring: require per-model latency, per-route cost, evict rates for cache, pod OOM events. Add export dashboards to their Grafana; provide alert recipes: p50/p95 latency, request queue depth, fallback rate > 5% (tunable).

Prompt / model quality notes (from Mateo):
- Their training includes seasonal fruit images; model is finetuned to output structured JSON with fields: fruit_type, ripeness_score, defect_flags[]. Must validate schema strictly on ingress. We propose function-calling style structured output with schema enforcement.
- Mateo wants a regression test harness: store 1200 labeled images + golden prompts and run nightly evals (quality/regression alerts). Redwood Optimize suggestions could help with quantization/latency tradeoffs but need artifact export.

Open questions (to clarify with customer):
1) Control-plane reachability: fully offline bundle vs agent + restricted egress (what does legal prefer)?
2) KMS: can they create AWS CMK with cross-account policies for Redwood or do they want HSM-only?
3) Retention policy: default logs TTL vs long-term archival and billing for storage + retrieval?
4) Golden dataset access: can they share a masked subset for us to run pre-deploy evals? (privacy check.)
5) SLA expectations: they asked for 99.9% uptime — do they require an enterprise contract for dedicated capacity? Likely yes.
6) Firmware update cadence: how frequently will devices change prompt schema (affects cache invalidation strategy)?

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Priya: draft onboarding checklist and PoC blueprint + list of binary bundle requirements (ETA 2026-02-23).
- Ethan: run quick model artifact mem/cold-start smoke test on A10 (use provided 2B checkpoint) and capture OOM / latency numbers (ETA 2026-02-26).
- Jun: outline monitoring/alerting exports and Grafana dashboard templates + RBAC mapping for their dev/ops teams (ETA 2026-02-25).
- Mateo/Claire (customer): confirm KMS path and whether they can permit limited egress for control-plane agent (ETA 2026-02-24).
- Product: check if Redwood Private supports unsigned fully offline installs today; if not, product to capture gap and estimate engineering work (owner: Marisol, ETA 2026-03-05).

Notes to self / rough risk matrix:
- Biggest risks: KMS/HSM compatibility, fully-offline deployment complexity, and model artifact memory footprint.
- Low risk: schema enforcement via function-calling (we already support structured output flows).

Scratch reminders / prompt experiments (informal):
- Try a two-step flow: camera captioner -> compact prompt template -> model generates JSON. Keep prompt small. Example template: "IMAGE_CAPTION: {caption}\nCONTEXT: {device_id}, {timestamp}\nTASK: classify fruit_type|ripeness (0-1)|defect_flags (comma)\nRETURN: JSON"
- Evaluate using short context window (<=128 tokens) to minimize KV pressure.

Follow-up meeting: schedule 1-hour technical deep-dive w/ Mateo + infra folks; focus agenda: KMS + offline bundle constraints, latency smoke test review, and rollout timeline. Suggested slots: week of 2026-02-27.

Random quick jots:
- If we can't do fully offline control plane, offer "signed bundle sync" pattern: customer pulls signed runtime bundles from S3 endpoint (explicitly approved) and applies on their schedule. This reduces continuous egress and matches legal asks sometimes.
- Cost estimate: rough back-of-envelope for prod: 3 A100-like nodes (~reserved) + storage + monitoring = ~$$$ (need finance run).

End of scratchpad — keep iterative notes here.

---
Change log: 2026-02-20 initial notes by Priya; 2026-02-22 added smoke-test owner/ETAs; 2026-03-02 added product gap owner (Marisol).
